newsitem.title: UK: BRITISH COMMERCIAL RADIO INCREASES AUDIENCE SHARE.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH COMMERCIAL RADIO INCREASES AUDIENCE SHARE.

text.p: British commercial radio increased its share of the country's listening audience to 50.2 percent in the 1997 second quarter, pushing it nearly three percentage points ahead of the BBC radio stations, a radio trade group said on Friday.

In addition, the Radio Advertising Bureau said commercial radio posted record quarterly revenue figures in the second quarter, up 13.3 percent year-on-year to 87.5 million pounds ($139.2 million). The growth in advertising revenue reflected a 19.8 percent growth rate from national advertisers, the radio bureau said.

Commercial radio and the five BBC radio stations have see-sawed back and forth for the dominant position in British radio over recent years. The Radio Advertising Bureau noted the size of commercial radio's current edge in audience share.
"It's quite a significant gap this time, the three percent," a spokeswoman for the Radio Advertising Bureau told Reuters.
The BBC radio stations had a combined audience listening share of 47.4 percent in the 1997 second quarter.

Commercial radio's share was up almost one percentage point from the 1997 first quarter. On a year-on-year comparison, commercial radio increased to a 50.2 percent share from 49.3 percent in the 1996 second quarter. The BBC stations in the 1996 second quarter had a 48.6 percent share.
